name.text: Matrix from the image of the unit square

questiontext.text:
The unit square OABC, with A(1, 0), B(1, 1) and C(0, 1), is mapped by a matrix \(M\) onto the parallelogram \(OA'B'C'\) with \(A'({@Ap[1]@},\,{@Ap[2]@})\), \(B'({@Bp[1]@},\,{@Bp[2]@})\) and \(C'({@Cp[1]@},\,{@Cp[2]@})\).

Find \(M\).

\(M = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The columns of a matrix are where (1, 0) and (0, 1) go. A(1, 0) goes to \(A'({@Ap[1]@},\,{@Ap[2]@})\), so the first column is \({@transpose(matrix(Ap))@}\). C(0, 1) goes to \(C'({@Cp[1]@},\,{@Cp[2]@})\), so the second column is \({@transpose(matrix(Cp))@}\).

\(M = {@ta@}\). Check with B: \({@ta@}{@matrix([1],[1])@} = {@transpose(matrix(Bp))@}\), which is \(B' = A' + C'\).

questiondescription.text:
Matrices and Transformations: matrix from the image of the unit square

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.1: Find the matrix of a transformation from the images of the vertices of the unit square.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 14, Exercise B, Question 2 of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 5 (Metric), ed. P. G. Bowie, Cambridge University Press, 1969: the image given by coordinates instead of a figure, new matrices, randomised, with named feedback.

truefeedback.text: You wrote the images as rows. The image of A(1, 0) is the first column of \(M\), written downwards: \({@transpose(matrix(Ap))@}\).
Your columns are the right way up but in the wrong order. The first column is the image of A(1, 0), which is \(A'\).

node.description: B' used as the second column

truefeedback.text: \(B'\) is the image of B(1, 1), not of C(0, 1). The second column is \(C'\). (Check: \(B' = A' + C'\).)

falsefeedback.text: Your matrix sends (1, 0) to \(({@ans1[1,1]@},\,{@ans1[2,1]@})\) and (0, 1) to \(({@ans1[1,2]@},\,{@ans1[2,2]@})\). Column 1 must be the image of (1, 0), which is \(A'\); column 2 must be the image of (0, 1), which is \(C'\).
